DXC issue #3693 -- Vector element index out-of-bounds not leading to compile error
https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3693

WHAT TO LOOK FOR

`indices` is a uint3, so its valid element indices are 0..2. Line 16 reads
`indices[3]`. Nothing here is dynamic: the index is a literal.

FXC pane -- rejects it:

    error X3504: array index out of bounds

DXC panes (1.6.2112 and trunk) -- exit 0. The out-of-bounds element becomes
`undef` and is used as a StructuredBuffer index:

    call %dx.types.ResRet.f32 @dx.op.bufferLoad.f32(
        i32 68, %dx.types.Handle %g_vertices_texture_structbuf,
        i32 undef, i32 0)   ; BufferLoad(srv,index,wot)

Validation passes. Nothing downstream objects.

Clang pane (hlsl_clang_trunk) -- also exit 0; the same element becomes
`i32 poison` in the equivalent load.

WHY THE POSITION MATTERS. DXC has the diagnostic and it works -- it just is
not reached when the subscript is the INDEX OPERAND of another subscript.
Hoist the same access out and DXC rejects it:

    const uint oob = indices[3];      // error: vector element index '3'
    g_out[tid] = g_vertices[oob];     //        is out of bounds

CONTROL. Write the same element as a swizzle, `indices.w`, and all three
compilers reject it (`error X3018: invalid subscript 'w'` / `error: vector
swizzle 'w' is out of bounds` / `error: vector component access exceeds type
'const uint3'`). So no pane here is silent because it failed to compile the
source or does not support these resource types.

STAGE. The issue reports lib_6_6 raytracing; this is a compute restating,
because FXC has no raytracing profile at all. The construct is not
stage-specific: the raytracing original behaves identically on DXC (exit 0,
`i32 undef` reaching rawBufferLoad).
